correctness.rationale: For every m>0, the norm has weight W(t)=exp(-t^{m/2}) and moments m_j=(2/m)Gamma((2j+2)/m), giving the exact input K(m)^2=Gamma(4/m)/Gamma(2/m) by published Theorem 1.3. Put x=2/m: duplication gives K(2/x)^2=2^{2x-1}Gamma(x+1/2)/sqrt(pi). The log derivative is 2 log2+psi(x+1/2), derivative psi1>0, initial value -gamma<0 and limit +infinity, hence one strict global minimizer. Conversion to m reverses derivative signs correctly. Small-x log-Gamma expansion gives K(m)=(1/sqrt2)[1-gamma/m+(gamma^2+pi^2)/(2m^2)+O(m^-3)], approached from below; Stirling gives divergence as m->0. Independent 55-digit mpmath root returned x=0.1450347431666722513354589782140, m=13.7897993014103048741, K=0.69348357463966042675. Finite numerics corroborate, not prove, universal claims.
